simple.meaning: אַדֶּרֶת (ʼaddereth) is a Hebrew object word meaning “something ample (as a large vine, a wide dress).” BibleIQ follows the concrete thing through the verses where it appears.
simple.biblicalBackground: The occurrence trail begins at Genesis 25:25. The surrounding context includes family line, Israel.
simple.inThisVerse: In this verse, the tapped English word is source-aligned to אַדֶּרֶת (H155) in the Hebrew text.
simple.whyItMatters: Concrete words often carry patterns through Scripture because objects, animals, offerings, and created things are used repeatedly in worship, judgment, covenant, and narrative.

definitions.short: something ample (as a large vine, a wide dress)
definitions.full: H155. addereth אַדֶּ֫רֶת noun feminine glory, cloak — ׳א absolute Josh 7:24 ; אַדָּ֑רֶת Ezek 17:8 ; construct Gen 25:25 4 t.; אַדַּרְתּוֺ 1Kin 19:13 3 t.; אַדַּרתָּם Zech 11:3 — 1 glory, magnificence , of vine Ezek 17:8 (so Thes MV, but < adjective f. from אַדִּיר q. v.), of shepherds Zech 11:3 (or sub 2 ). 2 mantle, cloak (wide garment) of hair שֵׂעָר Gen 25:25 ; Zech 13:4 (as prophetic mantle, so perhaps 11:3 of shepherds = false prophets) compare of Elijah 1Kin 19:13 , 19 ; 2Kin 2:8 , 13 , 14 ; but טוֺבָה שִׁנְעָר אַדֶּרֶת (fine mantle of Shinar = Babylonian mantle — doubtless costly) Josh 7:21 , 24 (J) & (late) ׳א alone Jonah 3:6 .
